guidance.title: Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988, s.30 (criticism, review, quotation and news reporting)
17 U.S.C. § 107: Limitations on exclusive rights: fair use

contexts.use: One reduced poster or cover beside the Library's own review of that film, with credit and source.
strengths: Closest fit to criticism and review: the image identifies the work and edition being discussed in substantive, film-specific text.
Whole, unaltered image at no more than 600×900, so it does not substitute for a print or for the film.
Non-commercial site; credit and source shown.
weaknesses: Posters are creative works, which weighs against unlicensed use (US factor 2).
UK fair dealing under s.30 needs "sufficient acknowledgement"; that requires the artist to be named where known, and many artists are unidentified.
A licensing market for poster images exists; the assessment is not a clearance.

contexts.use: The same reduced image as a thumbnail on cards that link directly to the film's review.
strengths: Each card links to the review, so the image still serves identification of the reviewed work.
Display is smaller than on the profile.
weaknesses: Repeated across listing pages, the image looks more like navigation or decoration than review; this is the weakest regular context for copyrighted items.
Cards show less of the credit than the profile; the credits page and profile must carry it.

contexts.context: Homepage, collections index and collection headings
contexts.use: Linked thumbnails: the homepage "Start here" shelf, three thumbnails per collection tile and up to four in a collection page heading, each linking directly to that film's review. The three larger homepage images are limited to public-domain and openly licensed posters.
strengths: Each image links to the film's review, so it still serves to identify the reviewed work.
The largest homepage images carry no copyright risk (public domain or open licence).
Thumbnails are small and shown whole or cropped only at the edge for layout; the full image and credit are on the profile.
weaknesses: On the homepage and collection tiles the images also make the page more attractive, which weighs against the criticism-and-review purpose; this is the weakest context for copyrighted items and should be reconsidered if a rights holder objects.
Collection-tile and heading thumbnails are cropped to a common shape (object-fit: cover, top-aligned).

contexts.use: Lists each image with creator, rights holder, source and rights category; thumbnails, if shown, are small.
strengths: Supplies the acknowledgement that fair dealing expects, and a route for rights holders to ask for correction or removal.
weaknesses: A gallery of copyrighted thumbnails without review text has no criticism purpose of its own; text-only entries (or links to the profiles) are safer for copyrighted items.

contexts.use: WebP files are committed to the public Git repository that builds the site.
strengths: Files are reduced copies; public-domain and openly licensed items carry no extra risk.
weaknesses: Anyone can download the set of copyrighted images from the repository outside the review context; the fair-use argument does not travel with the files.
CC BY-NC-ND items require downstream users to keep the licence terms; the repository should state them.

contexts.use: The poster URL given as the image of the film or review in schema.org markup.
strengths: Points to the same reduced file; no new copy is made.
weaknesses: Invites search engines and aggregators to show the image away from the review, which weakens the review justification. Safer to limit to public-domain and open-licence images, or omit.

notUsed: Posters are not used as backgrounds, banners, page decoration or social-preview images. Every poster on the site links to the review of its film.
